business_problem: Deloitte's research team needed to integrate multimodal scientific data and train protein and chemistry models quickly enough to make AI-assisted drug discovery practical, but assembling the infrastructure, data graph, and multi-node training environment for those experiments was slow and complex.
solution_summary: Deloitte built Quartz Atlas AI on NVIDIA DGX Cloud running on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure to accelerate drug-discovery research. The platform combines BioNeMo services for structure prediction and molecule generation with Deloitte's own generative models, plus a knowledge graph linking multimodal scientific sources such as papers, proteins, antibodies, and small molecules. Researchers use DGX Cloud to train protein and chemistry language models, run multi-node experiments with far less setup effort, and rank compounds before refinement with MolMIM and other NVIDIA-supported models. The resulting pipeline lets scientists search and analyze 12 million nodes and 97 million edges of scientific context in seconds, then feed that context into prediction and generation workflows. By turning infrastructure setup and model scaling into a managed cloud workflow, Deloitte shortened experimentation cycles and let researchers focus on biomedical reasoning instead of cluster operations.

data_flow: Scientific text, graph, and experimental data are ingested into Deloitte's Atlas AI knowledge graph, used to train and fine-tune protein and chemistry models on DGX Cloud, and then fed into ranking and molecule-generation workflows that return candidate compounds and predictions.
business_outcome: Deloitte cut one model-training stage from four weeks to eight days, improved developer productivity by 50%, eliminated seven to ten months of multi-node setup work, and gave researchers a graph-backed generative AI platform that can search and reason over 5 TB of scientific context in seconds.
metrics: cutting training time from 4 weeks to 8 days
